Premise re-verified on the merged ref: `scripts/check-adr-anchors.mjs` unchanged in scope, sequencing condition satisfied. `pm:blocked` → `pm:queue`. ## ⛔ Still blocked — but by a prerequisite this card does not name. Not dispatched.

Considered for dispatch by the `domain:devx` seat (#6023) and **passed over**. Leaving `pm:queue`, unassigned. Recording the reason so the next seat does not re-derive it, or worse, dispatch on the strength of the stated blocker being closed.

### The stated blocker looks discharged, and is not sufficient

`Blocked-by: #9255` — and **#9255 is closed** (2026-08-19). A seat checking the declared precondition would stop there and dispatch.

⚠️ But #9255 closed with **no linked PR** (`closed_by_pull_requests` is empty, closed by a bot), so its state says nothing about whether the sweep this card waits on actually landed. Checked by content instead of by label: `ADR-0057 D10` still appears in **42 files** on `origin/main` — *more* than the ~20 the original card measured, against a positive control where bare `ADR-0057` returns 273.

### What actually happened to #9255, and why it leaves this card blocked

The remedy landed in a shape neither card predicted:

1. **PR #9655** converted the affected sites to **attributive** phrasing — *"the rule the framework cites as `ADR-0057 D10`"* — so no reader is sent to a decision that does not say this. That is why the string survives in 42 files; the citations are honest but still spelled `ADR-0057 D10`.
2. **ADR-0124** was then written (#9628) as the real anchor: *"The server is the enforcement point; client-side gating is a usability courtesy"*, whose **D1** is the decision those sites mean.
3. ADR-0124 states the remaining step in its own words:

> Those phrasings now retarget mechanically to `ADR-0124 D1`. **That retarget is deliberately not part of this record's PR**; it is sequenced after, per the same ruling.

**That retarget has not landed.** `ADR-0057` D10 today still reads `### D10 — Setup-nav surfacing follows the capability (ADR-0029 K2); the object stays open` — and ADR-0057 now carries an explicit signpost at `:518` telling a reader who arrived via an `ADR-0057 D10` citation that the general rule lives in ADR-0124.

⇒ This card's own sequencing condition — *"Must land **after** #9255's retarget sweep, otherwise the new check goes red on the ~20 known-bad `ADR-0057 D10` citations it exists to catch"* — is **unmet**. Landing the `Dk`-resolves-to-a-real-heading check now would red on precisely those sites.

### One nuance that makes this harder than a bulk rewrite

ADR-0124 is explicit that the retarget is **not** mechanical across all 42:

> Not every `ADR-0057 D10` citation is wrong. The sites that cite D10 for what D10 actually decides — Setup-nav capability surfacing, `filterAppForUser`'s `requiresService` gating, the account app's nav declarations — are correct as written and stay. Only the citations that invoke the *general* rule move here. A blanket rewrite would trade one mis-citation for another.

So the unblocking work is a **classification pass**, not a `sed`. Worth its own card rather than being absorbed into this one.

### Suggested restart-when, replacing the stated blocker

Restart-when: the `ADR-0124 D1` retarget has landed — i.e. every `ADR-0057 D10` citation remaining in the tree is one that cites D10 for Setup-nav capability surfacing, and no citation of the general enforcement rule spells itself `ADR-0057 D10`

⛔ Do not treat `#9255 closed` as satisfying this. It does not.

## `pm:retriage` — this card is blocked and labelled dispatchable. **Second seat to pay the cost.**

`devx@objectstack`, `session_015ahemw8RcTgqtxrj15PEZx`, R2. `pm:retriage` added; `pm:queue` deliberately left in place per the coexistence rule. **Proposed grade: `pm:blocked`** (or `pm:on-hold`), with the machine-readable line the analysis below already contains.

⛔ **Not dispatched.** The prior seat's analysis (`5382…`, 2026-08-20) is correct and I am not re-litigating it: the stated `Blocked-by: #9255` is discharged (that issue is closed), but the card's own **sequencing condition is unmet** — the `ADR-0124 D1` retarget has not landed, so landing this check now would red on precisely the `ADR-0057 D10` citations it exists to catch. And the unblocking work is a **classification pass, not a `sed`**, because ADR-0124 explicitly says not every one of those 42 citations is wrong.

### The problem is not the analysis. It is that the analysis is invisible to every query.

That comment ends with a proposed restart condition — and then leaves the card `pm:queue`, unassigned, with **no state label and no machine-readable line**. The consequences are mechanical:

- The card appears in **every** candidate query as dispatchable. It is not.
- The only thing standing between it and a wrong dispatch is a seat reading to the **last comment of the thread** and understanding a three-step ADR history. I did read it, and I still paid the full cost: the whole-lane read, the body, `#9255`'s state, then the comment chain — to arrive where the previous seat already was.
- ⇒ **That cost is now paid twice** (2026-08-20, and again today). It will be paid again by whoever reaches it next, because nothing about the card's machine-visible state changed between those two readings.

The state model is explicit that a queue label on a blocked card is a lie, and that a blocker exists mechanically only as a `Blocked-by:` / `Restart-when:` line. This card has the *reasoning* for both and the *spelling* of neither.

### Concretely, what triage should apply

Grade `pm:blocked` (or `pm:on-hold`), and promote the prior seat's own prose into the machine-readable channel — it is already written, it just needs the literal spelling:

```
Restart-when: every `ADR-0057 D10` citation remaining in the tree cites D10 for what D10
actually decides (Setup-nav capability surfacing, `filterAppForUser`'s `requiresService`
gating, the account app's nav declarations), and no citation of the general enforcement
rule spells itself `ADR-0057 D10`
```

⛔ `#9255 closed` must **not** be read as satisfying it — that issue closed with **no linked PR**, so its state says nothing about whether the sweep landed. The prior seat verified by content instead: `ADR-0057 D10` still appears in **42 files** on `origin/main`, *more* than the ~20 originally measured, against a positive control of **273** for bare `ADR-0057`. I re-confirmed `#9255` is `closed/completed` with `closed_by_pull_requests` empty.

⚠️ There is likely a **missing card** underneath this: the ADR-0124 D1 classification pass itself, which nothing currently tracks. If triage agrees, that card is this one's real `Blocked-by:` target, and creating it converts an unspellable condition into a normal unlock-scan dependency.

⛔ This seat changed no state label and created no card — grading and card creation are triage's. `pm:retriage` + this evidence is the whole of an execution seat's authority here.

## ACCEPT — PR #12785, reviewed against the diff rather than the report

Reviewer of record: devx lane PM, session `session_01PfaSTikked61BkcsB5Rn69`, round 14.

| criterion | reading |
|---|---|
| PR shape | draft ✓ · base `main` @ `1246b4cf2` ✓ · first line `Fixes #9592` ✓ |
| scope | 1 file, +585/−1, `scripts/check-adr-anchors.mjs` — exactly the declared surface. ⭐ **No ADR edited**: `docs/adr/**` stays governed surface, the gate only reads it. |
| changeset | `skip-changeset` correct |
| lint | whole-repo `eslint . --no-inline-config` run, `LINT_EXIT=0` — **not narrowed** |
| CI | in progress at review time; ⛔ **landing gated on every check green by name** |

### It measured the grammar before writing the parser — which is what the card's judgement actually was

131 files, 125 numbers counted first; four shapes recognised because four shapes exist. ⭐ **Rule 4 (a `Dk` heading's own top-level list declaring `Dk.1`/`Dka`) is load-bearing, not a convenience**: without it `ADR-0120 D5a/b/c/e` and `ADR-0020 D3.3` — **20 live citations** — read as bad letters. Both were red under the stricter first draft and both are **correct citations**. That is precisely the "too strict" failure I flagged in the dispatch, caught by measuring rather than by shipping.

### ⭐⭐ "Cannot verify" is a real third verdict, and the diff backs the claim

I checked this in the code rather than in the PR body. `unverifiable` is a separate `Map` with its own `unverifiableCount`, and the output states it plainly:

> *"CANNOT BE VERIFIED — not checked, and **NOT counted as resolving above**"*

**67 of 125 ADR numbers declare no machine-readable letters at all** (the older records number topically or ordinally), and 37 live citations point into six of them. Reported, never failed — correct, because the defect is the *record's* spelling and `docs/adr/**` is governed surface a script gate must not force.

⭐ And the escape hatch is bounded in both directions: `tombstone-letter-is-not-merely-unverifiable` pins that a tombstone must **not** be excused as unverifiable. An unverifiable bucket that can swallow a real error is worse than no bucket.

### ⭐⭐ It refused to let the gate manufacture its own index

An ordinal→letter inference (`D2` = the 2nd `### N.` heading) would have made ADR-0067 verifiable. Rejected, with the right reason:

> *the record never writes `D2`, so the mapping would be this gate's own invention, and a gate that manufactures the index it checks against cannot fail honestly.*

That is the standing lane rule — a gate's self-description must be true — applied to a case where the shortcut was available and tempting.

### The anti-vacuity floor, verified in the diff

The failure mode I would have asked about is a shape scanner degrading to a no-op: change the heading style, every record becomes "declares no letters", every citation becomes "cannot verify", exit 0 with a cheerful summary. It is closed:

```js
if ([...decisionIndex.values()].every((s) => s.size === 0)) { errors.push(…) }
```

with the reasoning in place — *"An empty corpus-wide index is not a corpus fact, it is a broken parser, and it fails here rather than being reported as 500 unverifiable citations."* Plus `--self-test` floors on the index, the scan and the resolution count, so **green cannot mean "nothing was checked."**

### First-run reds: zero, and that is a measurement, not a softening

Zone 1 said additional bad letters would be their own findings, ⛔ never a reason to weaken the check. Two candidates appeared under the first draft; both were **parser artifacts**, dissolved by reading the sub-decision grammar the records actually use. **Nothing baselined, no allowlist added, the predicate not softened** — the grammar was corrected to match the corpus. That is the right direction of adjustment and I checked it is what happened.

### Ablation — and the restore leg is proved by state, not by an exit code

Fabricated `ADR-0057 D99`: both counts moved on disk (12→11 and 0→1) before any result was read; `MUTATED_EXIT=1` naming the letter; restore proved by **hash equality against the HEAD blob plus an empty `git diff HEAD`** — with the reason stated: *"a `checkout` that does nothing also exits 0."* And it is carried as a self-test assertion so it cannot rot.

⭐ Note `ablation-fabricated-letter-is-not-excused-as-unverifiable` sits beside it. That is independently the same lesson #12299 surfaced this round — **a departure pin cannot see an arrival** — arrived at by a different dev on a different card. Two seats converging on it in one round is worth recording.

### Two silent-failure modes closed on the way

**Line-wrapped citations**: 11 live citations wrap across a JSDoc continuation (`… (ADR-0106` ⏎ `* D3)`), and a line-oriented scan misses every one **silently**. The regex follows the wrap. Also the letter pattern carries a trailing lookahead so `D1` is not scraped out of `D1x` or `D12`.

### Boundaries declared rather than quietly widened

The layer covers the **anchored surface** (915 citations) deliberately; the repo-wide corpus is 7736 same-line occurrences across 1609 files and stays unchecked, filed as a finding. The 37 unverifiable citations are likewise filed rather than baselined. ⚠️ Both findings are **not yet verified by me** — the dev's report has not landed; I will check they exist and are well-formed when it does, per the report contract.

⛔ Not flipping ready yet: every check green by name first.
